reason: The sources provide over 15 verifiable, multi-source claims about the nebula's extreme scale, luminosity, and unique features like the quiet black hole.
story: Located 160,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud, the Tarantula Nebula is the ultimate scale-breaker. Discovered in 1751, this monstrous star factory is roughly 1,000 light-years across—so large it makes the famous Orion Nebula look like a tiny spark. It holds the title of the most active starburst region in our entire Local Group of galaxies. Its core cluster, R136, is packed with 450,000 suns' worth of mass and contains the most massive stars ever discovered. The nebula’s luminosity is so extreme that if it were moved to the Orion Nebula’s distance from Earth, it would cover a massive portion of the night sky and be bright enough to cast visible shadows. Beyond its glowing filaments, it hosts the historic Supernova 1987A and a unique 'quiet' black hole. Astronomers believe its dense heart is a future globular cluster, currently in the chaotic process of being born.
angle: If the Tarantula Nebula were as close to Earth as the Orion Nebula, it would be bright enough to cast visible shadows at night.

claims.claim: The Tarantula Nebula is also known as 30 Doradus.
The nebula is located in the Large Magellanic Cloud galaxy.
Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille discovered the nebula in 1751.
The nebula is approximately 160,000 light-years away from Earth.
It is the most active starburst region known in the Local Group.
The nebula is approximately 1,000 light-years in diameter.
If the nebula were at the distance of the Orion Nebula, it would cast visible shadows.
The nebula's central star cluster is called NGC 2070.
NGC 2070 contains a compact concentration of stars known as R136.
The Tarantula Nebula contains the most massive stars currently known to science.
The cluster NGC 2070 has an estimated mass of 450,000 solar masses.
Astronomers believe the central cluster will eventually become a globular cluster.
The nebula was named for its filaments that look like the legs of a spider in photographs.
Supernova 1987A occurred on the outskirts of the Tarantula Nebula.
A nine-solar-mass, X-ray quiet black hole called VFTS 243 was discovered in the nebula.
The nebula sits on the leading edge of its galaxy where gas compression triggers star formation.

disputed: The exact diameter ranges from 650 to over 1,860 light-years; scripts should use 'about 1,000' as a consensus estimate.
The telescope used for discovery is described as a 1/2-inch refractor or a 2-foot telescope; attribute generally to a 'small telescope'.
The nebula's location in the LMC is cited as both the south-east corner and the northeastern edge; describe it simply as being within the LMC.
The exact distance varies between 160,000 and 170,000 light-years across sources; use 'roughly 160,000'.
